name: Arizona
basePeriod: The first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before your claim. Arizona has no general alternate base period.
notModeled: The weeks rise from 24 to 26 when Arizona's unemployment rate for the prior quarter is 5% or more.

citation.sourceNote: A.R.S. 23-779: the weekly amount is "1/25 of the person's total wages" in the high quarter, "rounded to the nearest dollar, with an even one-half dollar being rounded to the next higher multiple of $1", at most $320. 23-771: a high quarter of "three hundred ninety times the minimum wage" ($15.15 in 2026, so $5,908.50) and a total of 1.5 times it, or wages in two quarters, one enough for the maximum, totaling the $8,000 wage base. DES: "The minimum weekly amount is $236, the maximum is $320." 23-780: 26 weeks if the prior quarter's unemployment rate is 5% or more, 24 if under, and never more than "one-third of the individual's base period earnings"; DES states 24. Arizona pays no dependent allowance. Read 2026-10-19.
